inspection.title: Vehicle Inspection
inspection.subtitle: Information about vehicle inspection — when, how, and what happens.
inspection.whenTitle: When should your car be inspected?
inspection.whenP1: The first inspection for passenger and delivery vehicles must be carried out no later than the day four years have passed from the date of first registration.
inspection.whenP2: After that, inspections are performed every two years until ten years have passed from the registration date. Cars ten years and older are inspected annually.
inspection.whenP3: Motorhome inspection schedules follow the same rules as passenger cars. Caravans with a total mass of 750 kg or less do not require inspection.
inspection.whenP4: You can check your inspection date easily through Trafi's online service or from your vehicle's registration certificate.
inspection.whatP1: You can be present during the inspection or wait in the office. You can also drop off your car in the morning and pick it up in the evening.
inspection.checksTitle: During the inspection, the following are checked:
inspection.checksExtra: Additionally, payment of vehicle-related taxes and fees is monitored during the inspection.
inspection.failTitle: What if the car fails inspection?
inspection.failP1: Based on a defect found during inspection, the car may be ordered for a re-inspection. The re-inspection must be completed within one month of the periodic inspection.
inspection.failP2: For minor defects, only a repair recommendation may be issued, meaning the car does not need to be re-approved.
inspection.failP3: A vehicle may not be used in traffic if it has not been inspected or if it has been placed under a driving ban during inspection.
inspection.deregisteredTitle: If the car has been deregistered?
inspection.deregisteredP1: The car can still be inspected as long as it has traffic insurance and an appointment booked. The vehicle must have attached license plates or a transfer permit.
